statement: For any square-integrable real X and a<b with P(X<=a)>=p>0 and P(X>=b)>=q>0, Var(X)>=pq(b-a)^2/(p+q). Therefore Damron-Hanson-Houdre-Xu Theorem 1's two fixed-probability quantiles at separation c sqrt(log ||x||) imply a c' log ||x|| variance lower bound on Z^2 where finite.
assumptions: For FPP application: iid nonnegative Z^2 edge weights with F(0)<p_c and F(I)<oriented_p_c if I>0, as in arXiv:1810.08270v2 Theorem 1
proof_or_counterexample: Minimize p(mu-a)^2+q(b-mu)^2 over mu in [a,b]; outside [a,b] a one-sided bound is stronger. See REVIEW_PACKET.md L1 reproduction.
